scales.name: Restraint
scales.definition: Capacity to hold to an intention against a competing immediate pull.

facets.name: Cue resistance
facets.definition: Not acting on an available temptation.

facets.name: Follow-through
facets.definition: Continuing after motivation fades or something more appealing appears.

facets.name: Brake
facets.definition: Not saying or doing the thing in the moment.

bodyLinks.mechanism: Dopamine agonists produce impulse-control disorders — gambling, shopping, hypersexuality — in about 17% of Parkinson's patients, reversing on withdrawal.
bodyLinks.verification: Not verifiable at the individual level; the causal evidence is from drug exposure.

bodyLinks.mechanism: Serotonin function correlates inversely with aggression and impulsivity (r ≈ -.12 overall, strongest in pharmacological challenge studies), with tryptophan depletion raising aggression in already-prone individuals.

items.text: I've bought something within minutes of first seeing it.
items.informantText: They've bought something within minutes of first seeing it.

review.notes: SES confound: impulsive spending is only visible with money to spend. Check DIF by income band if collected.

items.text: I can have something tempting in the house and forget it's there.
items.informantText: They can have something tempting in the house and forget it's there.

review.notes: Reworded to remove a negation: agreeing with "I don't ..." makes the disagree side a double negative, which is a known source of respondent error. The pole and keying are unchanged; only the phrasing is now a positive assertion of the same thing.

items.text: I keep going well past the point I meant to stop — scrolling, watching, playing.
items.informantText: They keep going well past the point they meant to stop — scrolling, watching, playing.

review.notes: Deliberate overlap with the Block B reward-cue gain axis. This item asks about a stable tendency; the Block B version asks about magnitude of pull. Verify they separate; if not, drop this one and keep the gain axis.

items.text: When I set a limit for myself, I stick to it.
items.informantText: When they set a limit for themselves, they stick to it.

review.notes: High desirability — self-control is flattering. Retained as the cleanest direct statement of the construct; matched by c01/c03 at the opposite pole.

items.text: I've spent money I'd set aside for something else.
items.informantText: They've spent money they'd set aside for something else.

review.notes: Confounded with financial precarity — people on tight budgets raid savings from necessity, not impulse. Consider adding 'when I didn't need to' in revision.

items.text: When something I've given up is right in front of me, it stays easy to ignore.
items.informantText: When something they've given up is right in front of them, it stays easy to ignore.

review.notes: Reworded from "Being around something I've decided against leaves me unbothered", which was abstract on both halves: "decided against" is vague and "leaves me unbothered" describes an absence. The facet is cue resistance, so the wording now names a present temptation and a concrete response to it.

items.text: I've gone back to something I'd sworn off more than once in the same week.
items.informantText: They've gone back to something they'd sworn off more than once in the same week.

items.text: I gave something up years ago and have stuck with it, even when the pull came back.
items.informantText: They gave something up years ago and have stuck with it, even when the pull came back.

review.notes: Reworded from "I've held to a decision for years despite regular temptation", which was abstract on both halves — "held to a decision" names no decision, and "despite regular temptation" is stiff. The facet is cue resistance, so the recurring pull has to stay explicit (otherwise it reads as follow-through), and "years" carries the extreme severity.

items.text: I finish the dull remainder of a job rather than leave it.
items.informantText: They finish the dull remainder of a job rather than leave it.

review.notes: Boundary with a1_drive_f04 ('if something takes more work than expected, I drop it'). A1 is about effort cost; A3 is about a competing pull. If they load together, the facet distinction has failed.

items.text: I move to whatever's more appealing before the current thing is done.
items.informantText: They move to whatever's more appealing before the current thing is done.

items.text: I do what I said I'd do even when I no longer feel like it.
items.informantText: They do what they said they'd do even when they no longer feel like it.

review.notes: High desirability. Kept because it is the definitional core of the facet; will be first cut if Pilot 1 shows a strong desirability correlation.

items.text: I have several things part-finished right now because something else pulled me away.
items.informantText: They have several things part-finished right now because something else pulled them away.

review.notes: Overlaps the ADHD flag in Block C. Distraction-driven non-completion should route there rather than inflate low Restraint; check the correlation with the ASRS-style items.

items.text: Once I commit to a plan, I stay with it even when a better offer appears.
items.informantText: Once they commit to a plan, they stay with it even when a better offer appears.

review.notes: Reworded to remove a negation: agreeing with "I don't ..." makes the disagree side a double negative, which is a known source of respondent error. The pole and keying are unchanged; only the phrasing is now a positive assertion of the same thing.

items.text: My attention goes where it wants regardless of what I'd planned.
items.informantText: Their attention goes where it wants regardless of what they'd planned.

review.notes: Also an ADHD-flag boundary case. See f04.

items.text: People have stopped relying on me to finish what I take on.
items.informantText: People have stopped relying on them to finish what they take on.

items.text: I've completed long commitments that most people around me abandoned.
items.informantText: They've completed long commitments that most people around them abandoned.

review.notes: High desirability and requires opportunity (long commitments are not equally available). Flagged for both desirability and SES checks.

items.text: I've said something in the moment that cost me later.
items.informantText: They've said something in the moment that cost them later.

items.text: I can hold my tongue when it matters.
items.informantText: They can hold their tongue when it matters.

review.notes: Directness norms vary by culture; holding back is valued unevenly. DIF-test by locale.

items.text: I react first and think it through afterwards.
items.informantText: They react first and think it through afterwards.

items.text: In an argument I can stop myself from saying the thing that would win it.
items.informantText: In an argument they can stop themselves from saying the thing that would win it.

review.notes: Boundary with A5 Antagonism: this measures the brake, not the motive. Someone low in Antagonism has nothing to hold back, which may produce a ceiling effect — watch the distribution.

items.text: I send messages I later wish I'd slept on.
items.informantText: They send messages they later wish they'd slept on.

items.text: When I'm angry there's a gap between feeling it and acting on it.
items.informantText: When they're angry there's a gap between feeling it and acting on it.

items.text: Acting on impulse has cost me a job, a relationship or a lot of money.
items.informantText: Acting on impulse has cost them a job, a relationship or a lot of money.

review.notes: Double-barrelled by design (three outcomes, one construct: serious consequence). Cognitive interviews must confirm respondents read it as 'any of these' rather than 'all of these'; split if not.

items.text: Even under real provocation, I don't do anything I'll regret.
items.informantText: Even under real provocation, they don't do anything they'll regret.

review.notes: High desirability, extreme high-pole. The provocation framing matters: testosterone and serotonin effects on behavior appear specifically under provocation, so this is the item closest to the mechanism literature.

citations.title: DOMINION study: impulse control disorders in Parkinson's disease
citations.claim: Impulse control disorders occur in about 17% of Parkinson's patients taking a dopamine agonist, 2-3x the rate of those not taking one.

citations.title: Revisiting the serotonin-aggression relation in humans: a meta-analysis
citations.claim: Central serotonin function correlates inversely with aggression, anger and hostility (r = -.12; r = -.21 in pharmacological challenge studies).
